text: Bonaya Adhi Godana, born on September 2, 1952, in Dukana, Kenya, and who passed away on April 10, 2006, in Marsabit, Kenya, served as Kenya's foreign minister from January 1998 until 2001. From 2002 until his death, he held the position of deputy leader of the opposition Kenya African National Union (KANU) party and was the Member of Parliament for North Horr Constituency. He died in a Kenya Air Force plane crash near Marsabit on April 10, 2006, in which 13 other people were killed and three survived. Among the victims were several government officials, including two assistant cabinet ministers who were political rivals of Godana. The group, consisting of politicians and religious leaders, was on a mission to secure peace along the Ethiopian border. A decade earlier, on July 28, 1996, he had survived a helicopter crash at the same Marsabit airstrip. Godana earned a Master of Law degree from the University of Nairobi in 1976 and a PhD in International Law from the Graduate Institute of International Studies in Geneva in 1984.
